summary: Up 0.1 from w11 (8.3). Two of the w11 blockers moved. (1) The second seat trim is the biggest gain. The centre-block aisle seats (D/G) now have petal backs and cushions with dash-weave ears (q13 centre seat, p3 quad A-B-B-A-style ends), so q13 can finally match the py_37302 foreground. Window pairs stay trim A (q14, p8), as py_37301 shows. (2) The literature pocket is now an open tray. It is about 0.69-0.76 of the bezel width (was 0.94), the recess is dark, and the smile rim dips at the centre (p2/p6/q13b). The Lego bricks in the q13b foreground and p5 cushions are gone, and the ears are broader and flatter. Three things keep it below 8.5. (a) The calmer-cloth change overshot. At studio or mid range the trim-A back is a soft, blurred melange: p8 back p10/p50 0.83, p90/p50 1.19, high-pass SD 0.12, against py_37301 0.71 / 1.25 / 0.18. The crisp pale-blue block mosaic of py_37301 / 37303 is lost (montage scratchpad w12b/fab_montage.png). (b) Petal chips on both trims render as small, round, evenly spaced white dots. py_37302's foreground back and san_12 show elongated (about 2-3:1), angular, cream-grey slivers at roughly twice the area cover. The py_37305 ear shows notched sakura chips whose largest are about 25 % bigger than ours. (c) In the pocket, the mesh is still a straight black rectangle with square ends, with about 5 cm of plain grey tray face between the smile rim and the mesh. In b_san_26 the rim sits directly on a mesh whose bottom follows the rounded bulge. Smaller items: the gooseneck hose is still thin (0.34 of the head, against 0.5-0.67), the bezel is pure black #060708 against #282932 / #161621 in py_37304, and the cushion is desaturated (S 0.10 against 0.17).
lighting_note: Not scored. The sun diamond on the q14 26A back is still there. The q13/q14 cabin renders the PY cloth about 25 % darker than py_37301 (p8 back mean #697285 against #8f9cb3 in the studio, too), and the cushions wash toward neutral grey-white in q13/q14 (p8 cushion S 0.10 against 0.17). The q13b foreground navy band and the magnified fabric come from the camera sitting inside the seat ahead, so they are not scored.

issues.issue: The trim-A back and cushion weave overshot into a blurred, low-contrast melange. At studio and cabin distance the crisp pale-blue / slate block mosaic of the official photos is gone. The back reads as soft horizontal smears, the darks are too light and the high-frequency detail is about 2/3 of the photo's.

issues.fix: test/make_swatches.py synth_py_back, keeping the tapered ends: (1) the thread modulation darkens the blocks by about 40 %: change `lite *= 0.45 + 0.85 * thr` to `lite *= 0.7 + 0.45 * thr` and `dark *= 0.7 + 0.4 * thr` to `dark *= 0.85 + 0.25 * thr`. (2) Sharpen the block bands: the light band divisor /2.0 -> /1.3 and the dark /1.0 -> /0.8. Keep the seg taper /3.0. (3) `out = (1 + 1.4 * lite) * (1 - 0.6 * dark)` -> `(1 + 1.5 * lite) * (1 - 0.68 * dark)`. (4) blk sigma 0.15 -> 0.18 so the 2x2 light/dark patches show. Re-cut and check that the p8 back reaches p10/p50 about 0.72-0.75, p90/p50 1.25-1.30 and high-pass SD 0.17-0.19.

issues.issue: Petal chips (tex_py_confetti, used on the trim-A ears and the trim-B back and cushion) render as small round, evenly spaced, pure-white dots ('snow'). Official and real photos show elongated angular slivers / sakura chips in cream-grey, denser on the trim-B back, with a wider size spread.
issues.evidence: py_37302 foreground back (crop w12b/p302_fg.png): slivers about 2-3:1, cream #b7ccec-ish, bright cover about 9 % against about 5 % on the w12 q13 trim-B back (same 1.45x median threshold). san_12 (26G): dense small angular flakes. py_37305 L ear: cover 0.150 and p90 diameter 0.071 of the ear width, against 0.115 / 0.056 in w12 p4. In p4 / q14 the facets of the 5-7-gon chips are not visible: they are below a pixel, so the shapes read as ovals.
issues.fix: test/make_swatches.py synth_py_confetti: elongation e uniform(1.2, 2.4) -> uniform(1.8, 3.2), with about 25 % of the chips given a two-lobed notch (sakura) at req 7-10; req normal(5.5, 2) -> normal(6.5, 2.5), clip 3-11; count 32 -> 44 with min spacing 24 -> 19 px; petal gain 6.5 -> 5.5 so the chips read pale cream-grey, not white; drop the 30 'mid-size specks' (they add the round-dot snow). Optional, if a separate tile is affordable: give the trim-B back (pyFabricB) a denser, smaller variant (0.07 m tile) so its slivers are finer than the ear chips, as in py_37302.

issues.issue: Literature pocket: the mesh is a straight black rectangle with square ends at the very bottom of the tray. issues.fix: src/09b_py.js pocket: rimY = 0.06 + 0.085 * ((x / 0.135) ** 2) ** 1.5 (centre 0.06, sides 0.145), and build the mesh like the tray front, as an x-loft across [-0.125 .. 0.125]. Each column's height runs from rimY(x) - 0.006 down to a bottom of 0.012 + 0.02 * (x / 0.125) ** 2, so the ends curve up. Use the same section count as the current mesh SEC loft (no net triangles).
